format.read: Read 'input' (UTF-8). With 'equivalent': also read that text and compare the two datum sequences with equal?. With 'types': the sequence read has exactly these types, in order.
format.read-error: Read 'input' (or the bytes of 'input_hex'). Reading MUST fail with the code 'error' at position [line, column].
format.read-positions: Read 'input'. For each entry, 'path' indexes the sequence read and then list elements (0-based); the node found MUST be in the position table with 'position'.
format.eval: Evaluate 'program' as a file (section 8.7), with only the library io available to import (section 8.9), with 'input' (or the bytes of 'input_hex') as standard input (empty if absent). Standard output MUST be exactly 'output'. With 'value': the program terminates normally, and the value of the last form is equal? to the datum read from 'value'. With 'error': the program terminates with an uncaught error whose :kind is the keyword 'error'. With 'error_position': the descriptor of that error has a :position whose :line and :column are the pair [line, column]; when it is null, the descriptor has no :position.
